tiering.rule: the tier-stop criterion is the disease DEG union resolved to the frozen 18,164-gene axis (axis-resolved, not genome-wide): a source DEG off the axis cannot enter DEG2000 or any axis built from it, so it does not count toward the 2,000-gene stop test. Sources are collected in ascending tier order; a tier with no declared source is absent from the ladder (AF declares tier 1 and tier 3, no tier 2), and a category whose evidence begins at tier 2 enters there. The cumulative axis-resolved union is measured after each tier and collection stops at the first tier whose union reaches the limit; a declared source in a deeper tier after a completed tier that already reached the limit is refused rather than admitted. Only declared sources are collected, so a tier between two entered tiers is never back-filled.
